subject: Support Backlog and Escalation Triage — MX-3 and GX-7

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: I asked for this because the backlog has gotten to a point where I can't triage it alone and a few things need decisions from people who aren't me. As of this morning I have 23 open tickets across MX-3 and GX-7. Fourteen are minor — configuration questions, documentation gaps, stuff I can close without involving anyone. Nine are substantive.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Which customers are in the nine?

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: Quennick has three open. Trellisar has two. Hessanby Dynamics has two — they're new to the platform and both of theirs are setup-related, so I'm not worried about those. And then there are two from Ivelmoor Group that have been open longer than I'm comfortable with.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Ivelmoor. What are those?

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: First one is a GX-7 unit that's reporting intermittent communication timeouts on the RS-485 bus. Customer says it started after they reorganized their panel wiring about six weeks ago. I've been working them through cable length and termination checks but we haven't resolved it. Second one is a firmware question — they asked whether the GX-7 supports a specific register read interval shorter than 500 milliseconds, and I don't have a definitive answer.

turns.speaker: Sofia
turns.text: On the register read interval — what's the specific interval they're asking about?

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: They want 200 milliseconds.

turns.speaker: Sofia
turns.text: The firmware scheduler runs at 250-millisecond resolution in the current release. 200 milliseconds is not achievable without a firmware change. I can give you a written answer for the ticket.

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: That would help. Can you get it to me today?

turns.speaker: Sofia
turns.text: Yes. I'll write it up so you can send it verbatim.

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: The RS-485 timeout issue — Devon, is there anything on the hardware side I should be walking them through that I might be missing? I've covered termination resistors and cable length. What else?

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: Ground potential difference is the one that bites people after a rewire. If they moved cables and crossed panel sections, the ground reference between the GX-7 and the downstream device might have shifted. Ask them to measure the ground voltage between the GX-7 chassis and the RS-485 device chassis with a meter. If it's more than a couple of volts, that's your problem.

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: I would not have thought of that. I'll add it to the ticket today.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Ivelmoor is a $90,000 account. I'd like both of those tickets closed before end of next week. Theo, will that be possible?

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: With Sofia's answer on the register question, yes, that one closes fast. The RS-485 issue depends on how quickly Ivelmoor's team can do the ground check. I'll push for it.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Let me know if you need me to make a call to their project lead. I'd rather involve myself early than have it escalate.

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: I'll try the technical path first. If Ivelmoor doesn't respond by Thursday, I'll flag you.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Good. What about the Quennick tickets?

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: Two of the three are related. Quennick has MX-3 units in a facility where ambient temperature runs high — they said up to 48 degrees Celsius in summer. They're asking whether the MX-3 is rated for that and whether there are any operational limitations they should know about.

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: The MX-3 is rated to 55 degrees Celsius operating, so 48 is within spec. But I'd want to flag that sustained operation above 45 degrees will shorten capacitor life on the power board — it's within spec but it's toward the top of the comfortable range. I'd recommend they ensure airflow around the unit.

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: Is there documentation I can send them or do I need to write something up?

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: The operating temperature range is in the datasheet. The capacitor life guidance isn't written down anywhere formal. I can put together a short application note — probably a page — that covers high-temperature deployment recommendations.

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: That would be very useful, not just for Quennick but for any customer in a hot environment. Can you have it in two weeks?

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: Two weeks is fine.

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: Quennick's third ticket is actually a firmware question. They're asking whether MX-3 firmware 2.4.1 will be supported past end of year or whether they need to plan an upgrade. Sofia, do we have a published support lifecycle for firmware versions?

turns.speaker: Sofia
turns.text: We don't have a published policy. Internally, I've been maintaining 2.4.x with patches as needed, but I haven't committed to a public end-of-life date. That's a policy question, not a technical one.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Quennick will not accept 'we don't have a policy' as an answer. They have procurement and IT governance requirements. They need something in writing.

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: What should I tell them in the meantime?

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Tell them we're formalizing the lifecycle policy and will have a written commitment to them within thirty days. That buys us time without closing a door.

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: I can send that. Sofia, can you actually have a draft lifecycle policy ready in that window?

turns.speaker: Sofia
turns.text: A draft, yes. Whether it goes through Priya and Callum and gets approved in thirty days — that I can't promise.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Let's start the clock anyway. If it slips, I'll manage Quennick.

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: Trellisar — their two tickets are both GX-7. One is a question about whether we support Modbus TCP in addition to RTU. The other is a hardware thing: they say one of their units has a status LED that's dimmer than the others. Not off, just noticeably dimmer.

turns.speaker: Sofia
turns.text: Modbus TCP — the GX-7 supports RTU only in the current firmware. TCP is on the roadmap but I can't commit to a release date.

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: The dim LED could be a resistor tolerance issue on that specific unit, or it could be the LED itself. It's cosmetic — it doesn't affect function. If Trellisar wants a replacement unit, we should just swap it and take the return.

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: They haven't asked for a replacement. They just reported it. Should I proactively offer one?

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Yes. Offer it. It costs us one unit and it signals that we stand behind the hardware. Trellisar is a growth account.

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: I can pull a replacement from finished goods stock and have it shipped this week if Theo sends me the request.

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: Done. I'll send you the shipping details today.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: How many GX-7 units do we have in finished goods right now, by the way?

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: As of Monday's count, 34 units.

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: Last thing — I want to flag a pattern I'm seeing. Seven of my 23 tickets involve questions that should be answerable from the documentation but aren't, because the docs are incomplete or outdated. Static IP configuration, Modbus register maps, operating environment specs. I'm spending time answering questions that the manual should handle. I'm not sure what the fix is, but someone should know it's happening.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: That's a real cost. Every ticket Theo answers manually is time not spent on new customers.

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: The register map I can update — I have a current version that never made it into the customer-facing docs. I'll get it to Theo.

turns.speaker: Sofia
turns.text: I can do the same for the firmware-related sections. Give me a list of what's missing, Theo, and I'll prioritize it.

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: I'll pull together a gap list from the tickets and send it to both of you by end of week.

decisions: Elena will contact Ivelmoor's project lead if Theo has not received a response on the RS-485 issue by Thursday.
Quennick will be told that a formal firmware lifecycle policy will be provided in writing within thirty days.
A replacement GX-7 unit will be proactively offered to Trellisar for the dim LED issue and shipped this week.

action_items.task: Write up a definitive answer on the GX-7 200ms register read interval limitation for Theo to send to Ivelmoor today.
Add the ground potential difference troubleshooting step to the Ivelmoor RS-485 timeout ticket.
Write a one-page high-temperature deployment application note for the MX-3 within two weeks.
Draft a firmware version lifecycle and support policy within thirty days for Priya and Callum to review.
Send Devon the Trellisar shipping details today so the replacement GX-7 unit can be dispatched this week.
Send Theo the current GX-7 Modbus register map for inclusion in customer-facing documentation.
Compile a documentation gap list from open tickets and send it to Sofia and Devon by end of week.
